security_audit.summary: Adjudicated all 66 static findings as false positives. This is an auto-generated reference-documentation skill for the CCXT cryptocurrency trading library, consisting solely of Markdown files with no executable scripts. Every flagged pattern (Python HTTP libraries, system reconnaissance, at-command scheduling, hidden file access) matched natural-language documentation prose rather than active code, and no prompt-injection or data-exfiltration intent was found. The one unscanned file, SKILL.md, was manually reviewed and confirmed benign — its frontmatter parse failed only because of a translation prefix line.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md frontmatter could not be parsed by the static scanner (invalid_frontmatter).
remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line so the YAML frontmatter block starts on the first line of the file. This lets automated tooling parse the skill metadata correctly.

remediation.issue: The skill description and summary fields in the source metadata contain a raw 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' marker instead of a clean description.
remediation.suggestion: Populate the skill description with the intended text (for example, the CCXT summary from the frontmatter) rather than leaving the translation placeholder.

content.user_title: Build Crypto Exchange Integrations with CCXT
content.value_statement: Connecting to many cryptocurrency exchanges means learning each one's unique API. This skill provides unified CCXT documentation so you can fetch market data, place orders, and manage accounts across 150+ exchanges with one consistent interface.
actual_capabilities: Explains the unified CCXT API for fetching tickers, order books, OHLCV candles, and trades.
Guides order creation, cancellation, and management, including market, limit, and reduceOnly orders.
Documents exchange configuration such as API credentials, rate limiting, and custom HTTP headers.
Covers spot, swap, and perpetual futures trading concepts and their differences.
Describes error handling for exchange exceptions, network errors, and rate-limit responses.
Provides CCXT Pro WebSocket usage for real-time streaming market and account data.
limitations: This skill is documentation only; it does not execute trades or connect to any exchange.
It does not contain live market data, prices, or account information.
Exchange-specific behavior may change over time and should be verified against current CCXT releases.
It does not provide financial advice or trading strategies.

use_cases.title: Automate market data collection
use_cases.description: A developer wants to pull order books and candles from several exchanges using one interface. This skill explains the unified fetch methods and their return structures.

use_cases.title: Build an order execution service
use_cases.description: An engineer needs to place and manage orders programmatically. This skill documents createOrder parameters, order types, and cancellation methods.

use_cases.title: Learn crypto trading APIs
use_cases.description: A newcomer wants to understand how exchange APIs work. This skill offers getting-started guidance and clear explanations of core trading concepts.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch market data
prompt_templates.prompt: Using CCXT, show me how to fetch the current ticker and order book for BTC/USDT from Binance.

prompt_templates.title: Place a limit order
prompt_templates.prompt: How do I create a limit buy order for 0.01 BTC on Kraken using CCXT in Python?

prompt_templates.title: Handle rate limits and errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to enable CCXT rate limiting and handle exchange and network exceptions gracefully in a loop.

prompt_templates.title: Stream real-time data with CCXT Pro
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to use CCXT Pro WebSocket methods to watch the order book and open orders in real time, and explain the difference from the REST methods.

output_examples.input: How do I fetch the ticker for ETH/USDT?
output_examples.output: The skill explains that you call the unified fetchTicker method with the symbol. It describes the ticker structure returned, including last price, bid, ask, high, low, and volume fields, and notes that you must load markets before querying.

output_examples.input: What is the difference between spot and swap trading?
output_examples.output: The skill explains that spot trading exchanges assets for immediate delivery, while swap or perpetual futures use derivative contracts. It notes that swap amounts are measured in contracts, so the base amount depends on the contract size.

best_practices: Always call loadMarkets before querying symbols so the exchange metadata is available.
Enable the built-in rate limiter to avoid bans and stay within each exchange's request limits.
Store API credentials securely and never paste keys or secrets into shared logs or issues.
anti_patterns: Do not hard-code API keys directly in source files that may be committed or shared.
Do not ignore exchange and network exceptions; unhandled errors can leave orders in unknown states.
Do not assume all exchanges support every method; check the exchange.has capability map first.

faq.question: Does this skill place real trades?
faq.answer: No. It is reference documentation only. It explains how the CCXT library works but does not connect to exchanges or execute any orders.

faq.question: Which programming languages does CCXT support?
faq.answer: CCXT supports JavaScript, Python, and PHP. The unified API is consistent across all three languages.

faq.question: How many exchanges does CCXT cover?
faq.answer: CCXT supports more than 150 cryptocurrency exchanges through a single unified interface.

faq.question: How do I avoid hitting rate limits?
faq.answer: Enable the built-in rate limiter by setting enableRateLimit to true. This throttles requests so you stay within each exchange's allowed request rate.

faq.question: Can I stream real-time data?
faq.answer: Yes. CCXT Pro provides WebSocket methods for watching market data and account updates in real time. This skill documents those methods.

faq.question: Where do I set my API keys?
faq.answer: You provide API credentials when you create the exchange instance. The skill explains the required fields and reminds you to keep keys and secrets private.
